units.text: INT. RIVERBOAT COURTROOM - DAY
A county courtroom built into the old gambling deck of a paddle steamer, moored permanently at the levee.
Brass chandeliers.
Faded green carpet stamped with playing-card suits.
Through the tall windows, the brown river slides past.
MARGUERITE VOSS, 40s, defense counsel, navy suit, reading glasses pushed into silver-black hair, stands at the lectern.
At the other table, ELIAS THORNQUIST, 60, prosecutor, rumpled, a pocket watch chain across his vest, watches her with weary patience.
On the bench sits JUDGE PRUITT, 70, silver pompadour, half-moon spectacles, a gavel carved like a riverboat wheel.
BAILIFF KRAUSE, 30s, broad, stands by the door with folded hands.
On the stand, ILSA BRANDVOLD, 50s, a dock clerk in her Sunday best, twists a handkerchief.
Miss Brandvold, you've told this court you saw the lantern at ten o'clock.
units.name: VOSS

units.text: Yes, ma'am.
units.name: BRANDVOLD

units.text: And that you were certain of the hour.
units.name: VOSS

units.text: The ten o'clock whistle had blown. I always know by the whistle.
units.name: BRANDVOLD

units.text: The whistle at the lower landing.
units.name: VOSS

units.text: Yes.
units.name: BRANDVOLD

units.text: Which was taken out of service on the third of March.
units.name: VOSS

units.text: Brandvold's handkerchief stops moving.
Was it?
units.name: BRANDVOLD

units.text: The county ordinance is Exhibit Fourteen. The occurrence was the ninth.
units.name: VOSS

units.text: Your Honor, counsel is testifying.
units.name: THORNQUIST

units.text: Sit down, Elias. She's cross-examining. It's what the lady is paid for.
units.name: PRUITT

units.text: Thornquist sits.
He smiles slightly, almost to himself.
Miss Brandvold, was there a different whistle?
units.name: VOSS

units.text: The upriver one, maybe. From the cannery.
units.name: BRANDVOLD

units.text: Which blows at a quarter past.
units.name: VOSS

units.text: I may have been wrong about the time.
units.name: BRANDVOLD

units.text: A murmur ripples through the gallery.
Pruitt raps once.
Order. Mr. Krause, the doors.
units.name: PRUITT

units.text: Krause opens the doors; a breeze off the river lifts the papers on both tables.
Miss Brandvold, I don't want to embarrass you.
units.name: VOSS

units.text: You haven't, ma'am. I'd rather be wrong out loud than right and keep quiet.
units.name: BRANDVOLD

units.text: Voss takes off her glasses.
She lets that settle.
Nothing further.
units.name: VOSS

units.text: Mr. Thornquist?
units.name: PRUITT

units.text: Just one, Judge. Miss Brandvold. Whatever the hour, the lantern. You saw it.
units.name: THORNQUIST

units.text: I saw it.
units.name: BRANDVOLD

units.text: Where?
units.name: THORNQUIST

units.text: On the Hollis dock. Same as always.
units.name: BRANDVOLD

units.text: Thank you. That's all.
units.name: THORNQUIST

units.text: Your Honor, in light of the testimony, the defense moves to dismiss.
units.name: VOSS

units.text: Your Honor, the state withdraws the second count.
units.name: THORNQUIST

units.text: You're withdrawing?
units.name: VOSS

units.text: I'd be a fool to hold a case together with a whistle that doesn't work.
units.name: THORNQUIST

units.text: Counsel, approach.
units.name: PRUITT

units.text: They approach the bench.
Pruitt lowers his voice, but the room is small and the wood carries it.
Marguerite, I've watched you take apart three of Elias's cases this term.
units.name: PRUITT

units.text: Thank you, Judge.
units.name: VOSS

units.text: It wasn't a compliment. He lets you.
units.name: PRUITT

units.text: That's a lie, Walter.
units.name: THORNQUIST

units.text: It's Your Honor in my courtroom.
units.name: PRUITT

units.text: It's a boat, Walter.
units.name: THORNQUIST

units.text: Pruitt sighs and rubs the bridge of his nose.
Count two is dismissed. Count one will be heard Thursday. Mr. Krause, please escort Miss Brandvold out by the forward stairs.
units.name: PRUITT

units.text: Krause crosses to the stand and offers his arm.
Brandvold takes it, shaky.
I hope I didn't do harm.
units.name: BRANDVOLD

units.text: No, ma'am. You told the truth. That's the job.
units.name: KRAUSE

units.text: They exit.
Pruitt gathers his robes and steps down.
Voss and Thornquist remain, packing files.
Dinner at the Delta Queen?
units.name: THORNQUIST

units.text: You're buying.
units.name: VOSS

units.text: I'm always buying.
units.name: THORNQUIST

units.text: That's because you always lose.
units.name: VOSS

units.text: No. That's because I like the company.
units.name: THORNQUIST

units.text: She laughs, finally.
Together they walk out into the afternoon, past the dealers' cages now stripped to their brass.
The river keeps moving.
